(Currently Amended) A system for treating obesity, the system comprising: a gastric space filler comprising a first balloon connected to a second balloon by a conduit, wherein the gastric space filler is configured to occupy a substantial volume of a gastric cavity in the human patient in an inflated state; and an instrument throughput channel extending through the conduit, wherein the instrument throughput channel is configured to receive instruments, and wherein the conduit has an axial length that is greater than 5 mm.

(Currently Amended) The system of claim 32 wherein the conduit comprises a first lumen in fluid communication with the first balloon, a second lumen in fluid communication with the second balloon, and a third lumen defining the instrument throughput channel, and wherein the first and second lumens are configured to allow for independent fluid infusion into the first and second balloons.

(Currently Amended) The system of claim 33 wherein the instrument throughput channel extends along the axial length of the conduit, and wherein the axial length is configured to facilitate the passage of instruments.

(Currently Amended) The system of claim 34 wherein the gastric space filler further comprises a coupling mechanism configured to facilitate engagement with a retrieval device for removal of the gastric space filler from the gastric cavity via the esophagus, and wherein the coupling mechanism is described as a mechanism that allows for the retrieval device to connect and disconnect from the gastric space filler.

(Currently Amended) The system of claim 35 wherein the first and second balloons are made from at least one of the following: silicone, latex, polyethylene, polyurethane, and nylon, and wherein the materials are selected to provide flexibility and durability.

(Currently Amended) The system of claim 36 wherein the conduit comprises an inter-balloon section spacing the first balloon apart from the second balloon, and wherein the inter-balloon section has a length of about 10-40 mm. 

(Currently Amended) The system of claim 41, further comprising a delivery catheter configured to deliver the gastric space filler to the gastric cavity via an esophagus of the patient, wherein the delivery catheter is configured to receive the gastric space filler in a collapsed state, and wherein the delivery catheter is designed for ease of insertion and removal. 

(Currently Amended) The gastric space filler system of claim 42 wherein: the first lumen extends from the first end of the conduit to the first balloon; and the second lumen extends from the first end of the conduit to the second balloon, and wherein the first and second lumens are independently operable for fluid infusion. 

(Currently Amended) The gastric space filler system of claim 46 wherein the gastric space filler system is configured for delivery through an esophagus of a patient to a stomach of the patient, and wherein the system is designed to minimize discomfort during the delivery process. 

(Currently Amended) The gastric space filler system of claim 47 wherein the conduit is configured for attachment to a delivery catheter, and wherein the third lumen of the conduit is configured to receive an instrument passed through the delivery catheter, and wherein the attachment mechanism is designed for secure and reliable connection.
